question: does every file listed in every source receipt actually exist

normalisation.why: member names inside an upstream archive are not repository paths, so a list of them could never be checked; recording the extraction path makes every entry verifiable
normalisation.final_convention: tex_files holds archive member names; tex_files_repository_paths holds the checkable repository paths

finding.reading: no claim in the manuscript depended on a missing file, but the manifests asserted the presence of 190 files that were not there

repair.method: each affected archive was re-fetched from its recorded address and accepted only when its digest matched the recorded value, then re-extracted without overwriting existing files

secondary_result: this exercises the external-artifact policy on 16 sources rather than the 4 spot checks recorded earlier; every archive re-fetched at its recorded digest
now_enforced: source receipts are inside the reference scan, so a listed file that does not exist fails the gate on every run

gate_correction.issue: recording only repository paths broke a receipt contract that expects archive member names, and recording only member names left names that look like repository paths and fail to resolve
gate_correction.resolution: both conventions are recorded, and the reference scan was made structural so it trusts the key rather than the shape of the string, considering only values under keys that name a path
gate_correction.failing_first_test: a placeholder path was added under a path-named key and the gate fired
